post.caption:
India went from a cash economy straight to instant digital transfer, skipping cards almost entirely, with a printed square standing in for the whole terminal. The real change is not convenience, it is cost: when a payment costs close to nothing, payments too small to justify a card fee suddenly work. A five rupee transfer is not worth a card, it is worth a scan. The trade-offs are traceability and what happens when the network goes down.
